setup: sh evals/setup.sh <fixture> <run-dir> builds <run-dir>/repo, the agent's working directory.

evals.name: lambda-migration
evals.prompt: Queremos llevar el backend a lambdas, el plan está en docs/lambda-migration.md. ¿Tiene sentido en serio? Roastealo.
evals.expected_output: Verdict: no as written. Killers: the month-end export runs up to 22 min (ops/metrics) vs Lambda's 15 min max; the cost math uses 10 M req/month when real traffic is ~106 M, so Lambda costs ~$390/month vs $180 today. Also: 'stateless' is false (in-memory sessions with sticky ALB, socket.io WebSockets, export writes ~3 GB to local disk), uploads up to 48 MB exceed the synchronous payload limit, a 20-connection pool per function instance can exhaust RDS max_connections 200. Offers the boring alternative (stay on EC2/containers, maybe move only the export to a container task).

assertions.text: The first line after any title states a blunt verdict
Contains no emojis
Links an official AWS docs page for at least one Lambda or API Gateway limit
Flags that the month-end export (19-22 min in ops/metrics) exceeds Lambda's 15-minute maximum
Shows the plan's 10 M requests/month is ~10x below the real ~106 M and recomputes Lambda cost above today's $180
Refutes 'stateless' with concrete code: in-memory sessions (src/cache.js), socket.io WebSockets, or the export's local-disk writes
Flags uploads up to 48-50 MB against the synchronous invocation / API Gateway payload limit
Handles DB connections with evidence: either flags the per-instance pool / burst risk against RDS max_connections 200, or shows with numbers that it holds
Offers a concrete smaller or do-nothing alternative
Every killer/serious objection is backed by a file, a number from the fixture, or a doc; nothing contradicts the fixture
Flags that node-cron runs on both instances, so the export runs twice (changing the 19-22 min the plan relies on)
Tight: the answer is under 1,200 words

evals.name: prd-reminders
evals.prompt: Destrozame este PRD antes de que lo presente el lunes: docs/prd-smart-reminders.md. En data/ tenés lo que exportamos de analytics y soporte.
evals.expected_output: Verdict: not as written. Killers: SMS fallback for ~54k users without push is ~1.6 M SMS/month, ~$17k, near 40% of the $45k revenue ('SMS costs are small' is false); 'most requested' is false (3 of 215 Q3 tickets mention reminders); push on iOS/Android contradicts the non-goal 'no changes to the mobile apps'; ML model + SMS + dashboard + push in 4 weeks with 2 backend engineers. Serious: retention goal has no stated baseline (it is 18%) and the success metric (open rate) does not measure retention; the 21% vs 17% is correlation. Alternative: a cheap push send-time experiment on the existing reminder.

assertions.text: The first line after any title states a blunt verdict
Contains no emojis
Computes the SMS fallback cost (~50k+ users without push, daily, ~$15-20k/month) against the $45k revenue and refutes 'SMS costs are small'
Refutes 'most requested' with the ticket data (3 of ~215 Q3 tickets mention reminders)
Points out that push on iOS/Android contradicts the non-goal 'no changes to the iOS and Android apps'
Attacks the 4-week, 2-backend-engineer timeline against the scope (ML model, SMS, dashboard, push)
Says the success metric (open rate) does not measure the retention goal, and/or that the goal has no baseline (it is ~18%)
Offers a cheaper experiment or smaller version first
Every killer/serious objection is backed by the PRD or data/; nothing contradicts the fixture
Gives a short, ordered path of concrete changes that would make the PRD presentable on Monday
Tight: the answer is under 1,200 words

evals.name: solid-pr
evals.prompt: Roastealo: el PR es la rama feature/orders-customer-index contra main (la descripción está en el mensaje del commit). Lo quiero mergear hoy.
evals.expected_output: The PR holds up: composite index matches the query, CONCURRENTLY with knex transaction disabled is correct, evidence from EXPLAIN on staging. Says so plainly with no invented killer. Real weak spots: if CONCURRENTLY fails it leaves an INVALID index and IF NOT EXISTS makes a rerun silently skip it; tests only check the SQL string, not the planner; build time/IO on 41 M rows in prod.

assertions.text: The first line after any title states a blunt verdict
Contains no emojis
Does not claim a merge-blocking defect that isn't real; the verdict says it can be merged (possibly with caveats)
Does not claim CONCURRENTLY will fail inside a transaction (the migration disables it); recognizes the composite index matches the query
Mentions that a failed CONCURRENTLY build leaves an INVALID index that IF NOT EXISTS would then silently skip on rerun
Weak spots named are specific and true for this diff (e.g., tests only check SQL strings, prod build time on 41 M rows, no unique/other issue invented)
Tight: the answer is under 1,200 words

evals.name: microservices-neutral
evals.prompt: Te paso la propuesta de arquitectura que armó el equipo: docs/microservices-proposal.md. ¿Qué te parece? La idea es arrancar el mes que viene.
evals.expected_output: Even with a neutral prompt: a blunt no. The 38-min deploy is 31 min of serial tests and 4 min of uncached Docker build, not monolith size; 'each team deploys' with one team of 3 engineers; no scaling need (3.4 req/s peak, 12% CPU); reports is slow because of an N+1 (~18,000 queries per request) and a non-sargable date filter in src/reports.js; checkout's single DB transaction across inventory, orders and payments (src/checkout.js) would need sagas once split. Alternative: parallelize tests and cache Docker layers, fix the report query, maybe a modular monolith.

assertions.text: The first line after any title states a blunt verdict
Does not open by praising the proposal or the team; leads with what's wrong
Shows the 38-min deploy is mostly the serial test suite (31 min) and the uncached Docker build, not the monolith's size
Points out there is one team of 3 engineers, so 'each team deploys independently' has no teams to serve
Refutes the scaling premise: 3.4 req/s peak, 12% CPU, and the slow report is an N+1 (~18,000 queries per request) in src/reports.js
Flags that checkout reserves stock, creates the order and records the payment in one DB transaction (src/checkout.js), which splitting into inventory/orders/payments breaks
Offers the cheap alternative: parallelize tests / cache Docker layers, fix the report query, or a modular monolith
Every killer/serious objection is backed by the fixture; nothing contradicts it
Tight: the answer is under 1,200 words
